advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix or remove the column-based disambiguation in `resolve_symbol` since Ruff reports the `def`-keyword column, not the name column (the `name_col == column` match can never succeed).
evidence: name_col = child.col_offset + keyword_len + 1  (points at the function name, e.g. col 9 for a 4-space-indented def)
Ruff C901 location per ticket JSON: "location": {"column": 5, "row": 189} for `_dispatch` (points at the `def` keyword, col 5)
resolve_symbol: `exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]` — compares name-column to Ruff's keyword-column
advisory.finding: `resolve_symbol` disambiguates same-line candidates by comparing Ruff's `column` against an AST-derived function-NAME column (`col_offset + keyword_len + 1`), but Ruff's C901 `location.column` points at the `def`/`async` keyword, not the name. The columns never coincide, so the `name_col == column` branch can never select a candidate; the disambiguation path is effectively dead (it would always fall through to NormalizationError).
advisory.suggested_fix: Store `child.col_offset + 1` (the 1-based `def`/`async` keyword column, matching Ruff's `location.column`) instead of the name column, so the same-line disambiguation actually works; or drop the column branch and document that same-line defs are unreachable in valid Python.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a resolve_symbol test with two function defs on one physical line: assert the correct symbol is returned for each column and that a non-matching column raises the `ambiguous` NormalizationError.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:205 `exact = [qual for name_col, qual in candidates if name_col == column]`
scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:208 `raise NormalizationError(f"ambiguous function definition at line {row}, column {column}")`
tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py:303 `test_resolve_nested_equal_leaf_under_different_parents` uses `class A`/`class B` on separate lines — single-candidate path only
ABSENCE: no test constructs a source with two `def`s on the SAME physical line, so `build_symbol_index` never yields >1 candidate for a lineno and the column disambiguation code is unreached
advisory.finding: The `resolve_symbol` same-line disambiguation logic (the `exact`/column-match branch and the `ambiguous` NormalizationError, plus the `name_col = col_offset + keyword_len + 1` computation) is never exercised: all resolve tests use functions on distinct lines and hit the single-candidate early return. A bug in the column math or the multi-candidate selection would silently resolve a C901 finding to the WRONG symbol (mis-keying the baseline) and no test would fail.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a source like `def a(): pass; def b(): pass` (or use a lambda-free construct forcing shared lineno) and call `resolve_symbol` with each function's name column, asserting the right qualified name; also assert NormalizationError('ambiguous') for a column matching neither.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `_run_check` test that monkeypatches `run_scanner` (or `load_baseline`) to raise a BaselineError and asserts rc==1 with an `error:` message on stderr.
evidence: scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py:424 `except BaselineError as exc:` ... `return 1`
tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py has `test_run_check_reports_regression` and `test_run_check_allows_stale` only
tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py has `test_update_stale_refuses_on_scanner_error` / `test_update_stale_refuses_on_schema_error` for the sibling command but no `_run_check` equivalent
ABSENCE: no test drives `_run_check` with `run_scanner`/`load_baseline` raising a BaselineError to assert rc==1 and the `error:` stderr line
advisory.finding: The `--check` failure exit path (`_run_check` catching BaselineError and returning 1) is untested. Only the regression and stale outcomes of `_run_check` are covered; the sibling `_run_update_stale` has explicit scanner-error and schema-error refusal tests, but `_run_check` has none. A regression that swallowed a scanner/schema error and returned 0 would make the gate PASS on a corrupt baseline or missing ruff.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror `test_update_stale_refuses_on_scanner_error`: `monkeypatch.setattr(ccb, 'run_scanner', boom)`; `assert ccb._run_check(tmp_path) == 1` and assert the captured stderr contains `error:`.
